title: MetaVelvet Installation and Getting Started Guide
author: Afiahayati
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.d5k84v

steps.title: Download and decompress source tarball
steps.instruction: Download the MetaVelvet source tarball from http://metavelvet.dna.bio.keio.ac.jp/src/ and decompress it with the command: `tar zxvf MataVelvet-v1.1.01.tgz`.

steps.title: Clone source from GitHub (alternative)
steps.instruction: Alternatively, obtain the latest source code by cloning the GitHub repository: `git clone git://github.com/hacchy/MetaVelvet.git`.

steps.title: Enter MetaVelvet directory
steps.instruction: Change into the MetaVelvet source directory with: `cd MetaVelvet-v1.1.01`.

steps.title: Compile MetaVelvet executables
steps.instruction: Compile the program by running `make ['MAXKMERLENGTH = k'] ['CATEGORIES = cat']` where **k** is the maximum k‑mer size you wish to use and **cat** is the maximum number of read categories (i.e., number of libraries with different insert lengths). After a successful build, the executable `meta-velvetg` (version ≥ 1.1.01) will be created.

steps.title: Install executables
steps.instruction: Copy the generated executable(s) to a directory in your PATH, e.g.: `cp meta-velvetg /usr/bin/`. You may choose another install location if preferred.

steps.title: Download and decompress example dataset
steps.instruction: Download the small test dataset from http://metavelvet.dna.bio.keio.ac.jp/data/ and unpack it with: `tar zxvf HMP.small.tar.gz`.

steps.title: Run velveth to build k‑mer hash
steps.instruction:
Execute velveth to import reads and create the k‑mer hash table, checking that the files `out-dir/Sequences` and `out-dir/Roadmaps` are produced. Use a k‑mer size of 51 (recommended for reads longer than 65 bp):
`velveth out-dir 51 \
  -fasta -shortPaired \
  HMP.small/SRR041654_shuffled.fasta \
  HMP.small/SRR041655_shuffled.fasta`

steps.title: Run velvetg to build initial graph
steps.instruction:
Execute velvetg to construct the initial de Bruijn graph, ensuring the file `out-dir/Graph2` appears. Include the `-exp_cov auto` option (required for later meta‑velvetg) and specify the insert length:
`velvetg out-dir -exp_cov auto -ins_length 260`

steps.title: Run meta‑velvetg to generate scaffolds
steps.instruction:
Run meta‑velvetg to produce scaffold sequences, optionally providing the same insert length. Pipe the output to `tee` to save a log file and verify that `out-dir/meta-velvetg.contigs.fa` is created:
`meta-velvetg out-dir [-ins_length 260] | tee logfile`
